3175 .SH "OUTPUT FOR OTHER PROGRAMS"
 3176 When the
 3177 .B \-F
 3178 option is specified,
 3179 .I lsof
 3180 produces output that is suitable for processing by another program \- e.g, an
 3181 .I awk
 3182 or
 3183 .I Perl
 3184 script, or a C program.
 3185 .PP
 3186 Each unit of information is output in a field that is identified
 3187 with a leading character and terminated by a NL (012) (or a NUL
 3188 (000) if the 0 (zero) field identifier character is specified.)
 3189 The data of the field follows immediately after the field identification
 3190 character and extends to the field terminator.
 3191 .PP
 3192 It is possible to think of field output as process and file sets.
 3193 A process set begins with a field whose identifier is `p' (for
 3194 process IDentifier (PID)).
 3195 It extends to the beginning of the next PID field or the beginning
 3196 of the first file set of the process, whichever comes first.
 3197 Included in the process set are fields that identify the command,
 3198 the process group IDentification (PGID) number, the task (thread)
 3199 ID (TID), and the user ID (UID) number or login name.
 3200 .PP
 3201 A file set begins with a field whose identifier is `f' (for
 3202 file descriptor).
 3203 It is followed by lines that describe the file's access mode,
 3204 lock state, type, device, size, offset, inode, protocol, name
 3205 and stream module names.
 3206 It extends to the beginning of the next file or process set,
 3207 whichever comes first.
 3208 .PP
 3209 When the NUL (000) field terminator has been selected with the
 3210 0 (zero) field identifier character,
 3211 .I lsof
 3212 ends each process and file set with a NL (012) character.
 3213 .PP
 3214 .I Lsof
 3215 always produces one field, the PID (`p') field.
 3216 All other fields may be declared optionally in the field identifier
 3217 character list that follows the
 3218 .B \-F
 3219 option.
